breakthroughs: South of the matrix. Where the site must be in three to five years: few, bold and measurable, the reason for everything above them.
annual: West. What this year must reach on the way to the breakthrough objectives, each with a number and a date.
priorities: North. The top-level improvement priorities (projects, kaizen streams) that reach the annual objectives. Fewer is better: what is not here is not this year's work.
metrics: East. The metrics that prove each priority works, with the baseline and the target at year end. The monthly targets and actuals follow in step 4.
owners: Far east. The people who carry the priorities. Each priority needs one primary owner; secondaries help.

tips: Few objectives, deployed all the way.
Three to five breakthrough objectives, a handful of annual objectives, and every priority tied to an annual objective, a metric and one owner. What is not on the matrix is not this year's work.
Read the X around the clock.

Breakthrough objectives (south) lead to annual objectives (west), they to the improvement priorities (north), those to the metrics (east) and the people who own them (far east). Each corner says how strongly two lists hang together: ● strong, ○ weak.
Play catchball before the matrix is fixed.
The level below proposes how it will reach a priority, the level above answers, and a note says when both agreed. A priority nobody has agreed is still a wish.
Review every month on the bowling chart.
Each metric has a target for every month: met or missed, in words and in colour. Two misses in a row ask for a countermeasure with an owner and a date, and an A3 when the cause is not clear.
Let the projects carry the priorities.
Link a priority to its project in the Project Portfolio of this browser: its phase, status and savings show next to the annual objective it serves. The portfolio is only read here.
Pass the matrix down as a file.
Save it as a template file and send it to the next level; they open it here and build their own matrix under yours.

breakthroughs.text: First choice of our customers: 99.5% of orders on time in full by 2029
